topic.readerProblem: Work out what Trakkr really costs (plans, add-ons, annual billing, trial) and whether a small business should pay for daily AI-answer tracking.
topic.connection: Helps AEOeye readers decide between a one-time AI visibility baseline and a recurring monitoring subscription after they find a gap in AI answers.

assessment: The page is a documentation-based pricing guide for trakkr.ai: exact plan prices, add-on prices, annual and data-point arithmetic, trial and refund terms, and a stated small-business verdict (baseline first, pay only if AI answers cost you buyers and someone acts weekly). It rests on Trakkr's own pricing page, billing guide, FAQ and terms plus SparkToro and Pew research, and it deliberately makes no claim about Trakkr's data quality, hands-on use or outcomes.

sources.supports: Growth $100/month or $1,000/year, Scale $500/month or $5,000/year, Enterprise from $1,000/month billed annually, brands, prompts, seats, data points, 14-day card-required trial, 17% annual saving, billed in USD, and the Growth-vs-Scale depth-versus-breadth statement.

Add-on prices (extra brand $50, older $39; extra seat $20; extra prompts $39/$59/$99 per brand), plan feature matrix, annual billing equals ten months, trial conversion and upgrade-ends-trial rule, older subscriptions may keep earlier prices.
Eight tracked models, AI visibility definition, presence versus visibility score, 5 to 20 starting prompts, active-prompt rule, speed of change by engine, API-based collection, no free version.
Annual plans billed upfront and auto-renew, 14-day money-back guarantee for new subscribers, prices exclude VAT/GST, 30-day data export after cancelling.

Trakkr's robots.txt names GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, ClaudeBot, Claude-SearchBot, Claude-User, PerplexityBot, Perplexity-User, Google-Extended and CCBot with Allow: / (matches the AEOeye crawler access study row).
trakkr.ai publishes an llms.txt file at the site root (returned 200 and describes the company).
Definition of MCP (Model Context Protocol) as an open-source standard for connecting AI applications to external systems.

600 volunteers, 12 prompts, 2,961 runs on ChatGPT, Claude and Google AI; same list under 1 in 100, same order about 1 in 1,000; visibility percentage reasonable, ranking position unreliable; API-versus-user parity listed as an open question.
900 US adults, March 2025: link clicks on 8% of visits with an AI summary versus 15% without; 1% clicked a link inside the summary.
